gloss: sacred tree (at a shrine or temple)

definitions.gloss: sacred tree at a shrine or temple
definitions.explanation: A tree on the grounds of a Shinto shrine (or sometimes a Buddhist temple) that is regarded as sacred, often believed to house or attract a divine spirit. Typically marked off with a {注連縄|しめなわ} (sacred rope) tied around the trunk.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{御神木|ごしんぼく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{合|あ}わせた→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧。
examples.english: I put my hands together in prayer at the shrine's sacred tree.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{御神木|ごしんぼく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{樹齢|じゅれい}→樹齢：23245_jurei⟧⟦{千|せん}→千：00809_sen⟧⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{超|こ}える→超える：01942_koeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{伝|つた}えられている→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧。
examples.english: This sacred tree is said to be over a thousand years old.

examples.japanese: {御神木|ごしんぼく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{注連縄|しめなわ}→注連縄：06015_shimenawa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{張|は}られていた→張る：12583_haru⟧。
examples.english: A sacred rope had been hung around the sacred tree.

notes:
Compound of the honorific {御|ご} + {神|しん} (god, deity) + {木|ぼく} (tree). Often a large, ancient ⟦{老木|ろうぼく}→老木：28520_rouboku⟧ (old tree) believed to embody or attract a ⟦{神|かみ}→神：02147_kami⟧. Cutting or damaging one is treated as a serious taboo.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{御神木|ごしんぼく}: sacred tree of the shrine
- {御神木|ごしんぼく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{合|あ}わせる→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧: to pray at a sacred tree
- {御神木|ごしんぼく}⟦{信仰|しんこう}→信仰：03685_shinkou⟧: belief in sacred trees

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Shinto, certain natural features—trees, rocks, mountains—are considered to be {依|よ}り{代|しろ}, places where a deity can descend or reside. A {御神木|ごしんぼく} is one of the most common manifestations of this belief; it is marked with a ⟦{注連縄|しめなわ}→注連縄：06015_shimenawa⟧ and treated with reverence.
